rings.label: Adopt
rings.help: Use it. Stable, updated in the last 6 months, lots of people use it.

rings.label: Trial
rings.help: Try it. Still young (before 1.0), or quiet for 6 to 18 months, or few users yet.

rings.label: Assess
rings.help: Watch it. Brand new, less than a year old.

rings.label: Hold
rings.help: Avoid for now. Dead, deprecated, or no update in 18 months.

dx.title: Easy to use?
dx.explain: Is the tool easy for you, every day? Each check is 10 points. More checks: more to the right.

criteria.label: One command starts it
criteria.help: A single command brings up the whole thing it manages.

criteria.label: Little setup
criteria.help: Useful out of the box, or with a short generated config.

criteria.label: See changes fast
criteria.help: Live reload, file sync or incremental rebuilds in seconds.

criteria.label: Clear errors
criteria.help: Says what broke and how to fix it, or ships a doctor-style check.

criteria.label: Has a screen to look at
criteria.help: A web dashboard, TUI or desktop app, not only raw logs.

criteria.label: Working in 10 minutes
criteria.help: Official docs get a newcomer to a working result in about ten minutes.

criteria.label: Mac, Linux and Windows
criteria.help: Supported on all three, natively or through WSL.

criteria.label: No account needed
criteria.help: Runs on your machine without signing up or a network round trip.

criteria.label: Light and fast
criteria.help: Starts in seconds and does not need a large VM or many GB of RAM.

criteria.label: AI can drive it
criteria.help: An MCP server, a JSON output mode or an API an AI agent can drive.

parity.title: Made for big, real systems?
parity.explain: Small and simple: one service, nothing around it. Big and real: many services, real databases, containers, Kubernetes, the cloud, logs, big teams. Each check is 10 points. More checks: higher up.

criteria.label: Works with containers
criteria.help: Runs, builds or watches containers.

criteria.label: Handles many services
criteria.help: Brings up, connects or watches several services together.

criteria.label: Services talk to each other
criteria.help: Service-to-service networking, DNS or ingress like production.

criteria.label: Real databases and queues
criteria.help: Databases, queues or volumes, not only in-memory fakes.

criteria.label: Same images as live servers
criteria.help: Uses the images, bundles or lockfiles that production uses.

criteria.label: Speaks Kubernetes
criteria.help: Manifests, pods, Helm charts or a real Kubernetes API.

criteria.label: Works with the cloud
criteria.help: Emulates or reaches real cloud provider APIs.

criteria.label: Real config and secrets
criteria.help: Environment, config and secrets handled the way production handles them.

criteria.label: Logs, metrics, traces
criteria.help: Exposes telemetry the way production does.

criteria.label: Works for big teams
criteria.help: Built for many services and many developers sharing a setup.

roles.name: Backend Engineer
roles.what: Writes the APIs and services behind the app, and the database they use.
day: Builds and changes API endpoints
Writes database migrations and queries
Runs the service with its database and queue on a laptop

roles.name: Frontend Engineer
roles.what: Builds the screens people click on, and makes them fast and clean.
day: Builds pages and components
Calls APIs, or fakes them when the API is not ready
Fixes layout and speed problems in the browser

roles.name: Full-stack Engineer
roles.what: Builds the screen, the API and the database for one feature, alone.
day: Ships a feature from database table to button
Runs the web app, API and database together locally
Deploys and checks it in production

roles.name: Mobile Engineer
roles.what: Builds phone apps for iOS and Android, and wires them to a backend.
day: Builds screens and app logic
Points the app at a local or test backend
Tests on phones and fakes bad networks

roles.name: Java / JVM Engineer
roles.what: Writes server code in Java or Kotlin, usually with Spring or Quarkus.
day: Builds services on Spring Boot or Quarkus
Runs databases and brokers through Compose or Testcontainers
Tunes builds and fixes slow startup

roles.name: Python Backend Engineer
roles.what: Writes server code in Python, usually with FastAPI or Django.
day: Builds API endpoints and background jobs
Manages packages and Python versions
Writes tests that hit a real database

roles.name: .NET Engineer
roles.what: Writes server code in C#, often several services that talk to each other.
day: Builds APIs and workers in C#
Runs the whole app host with its dependencies
Writes database migrations with EF Core

roles.name: PHP / WordPress Developer
roles.what: Builds sites and apps in PHP, Laravel or WordPress.
day: Builds features in Laravel or a WordPress theme
Runs a local copy of the site with its database
Moves changes between local and live

roles.name: Ruby / Rails Engineer
roles.what: Builds web apps with Rails, from model to page.
day: Builds features end to end in Rails
Runs the app, jobs and database locally
Keeps gems and Ruby versions in order

roles.name: Serverless / Cloud App Engineer
roles.what: Builds apps out of cloud functions and managed services, with no servers to run.
day: Writes functions and wires them to queues and storage
Runs a fake cloud locally to test
Deploys with a few commands

roles.name: Student / Junior Developer
roles.what: Learning to code and ship. Needs tools that just work and do not break setup.
day: Follows tutorials and builds small projects
Fights with installs and versions
Learns git and how to read errors

roles.name: Indie Hacker / Solo Founder
roles.what: One person building a whole product. Wants cheap, fast and few moving parts.
day: Builds everything from signup page to billing
Uses hosted backends so there is less to run
Ships fast and watches for errors

roles.name: Founding Engineer
roles.what: First engineer at a startup. Does a bit of everything, picks the stack.
day: Picks the stack and sets up the repo
Ships features, fixes prod, sets up CI
Talks to users and turns it into code

roles.name: Platform Engineer
roles.what: Builds the internal tools and paved roads other developers use to ship.
day: Builds templates and self-service tooling
Runs the developer portal and CI base images
Helps teams get a working local setup

roles.name: Site Reliability Engineer (SRE)
roles.what: Keeps production up. Measures it, gets paged, and fixes the cause.
day: Reads dashboards and traces when something is slow
Writes alerts and runbooks
Reviews outages and removes the root cause

roles.name: DevOps Engineer
roles.what: Connects code to production with pipelines, servers and automation.
day: Builds and fixes CI/CD pipelines
Writes infra as code
Helps developers deploy without drama

roles.name: Infrastructure / Cloud Engineer
roles.what: Builds and runs the networks, clusters and cloud accounts everything sits on.
day: Writes Terraform for accounts, networks and clusters
Plans capacity and cost
Patches and upgrades the base layer

roles.name: Kubernetes / Cluster Engineer
roles.what: Runs the clusters apps live on, and helps teams deploy to them.
day: Upgrades and fixes clusters
Writes Helm charts and overlays
Debugs pods that will not start

roles.name: Release Engineer
roles.what: Owns how code becomes a version people can install, safely and on time.
day: Cuts releases and writes changelogs
Signs and publishes packages and images
Fixes a release that went half wrong

roles.name: Build / Developer Productivity Engineer
roles.what: Makes builds, tests and local setup fast for every other developer.
day: Speeds up slow builds and CI
Fixes flaky tooling and caches
Makes new-hire setup take minutes

roles.name: Observability Engineer
roles.what: Builds the logs, metrics and traces so teams can see what their code does.
day: Rolls out OpenTelemetry in services
Builds dashboards and alerts
Keeps telemetry cost under control

roles.name: Data Engineer
roles.what: Builds the pipes that move and clean data so others can use it.
day: Builds jobs that load and reshape data
Runs databases and storage locally to test
Fixes pipelines that broke overnight

roles.name: ML Engineer
roles.what: Trains models and turns them into something an app can call.
day: Prepares data and trains models
Wraps a model in an API
Checks it still works after changes

roles.name: MLOps Engineer
roles.what: Gets models into production and keeps them running, cheap and watched.
day: Builds pipelines to train, test and deploy models
Runs model servers on a cluster
Watches cost, speed and drift

roles.name: AI / Agent Engineer
roles.what: Builds apps where an LLM calls tools and does multi-step work.
day: Wires an agent to tools, memory and APIs
Runs several agent services together locally
Traces runs to see why an agent went wrong

roles.name: Prompt / Eval Engineer
roles.what: Writes the tests that tell if an LLM app got better or worse.
day: Writes test cases for prompts and agents
Runs evals on each change and compares scores
Reads traces to find where answers go wrong

roles.name: LLM Inference / Local Models Engineer
roles.what: Runs open models on own hardware, fast and cheap.
day: Serves models behind an API
Picks model sizes and quantization
Measures speed and memory

roles.name: MCP / Agent Tooling Engineer
roles.what: Builds the tools and servers that let AI agents act on real systems.
day: Writes MCP servers around internal APIs
Tests them with an inspector and real agents
Handles auth and safe access

roles.name: QA / Test Automation Engineer
roles.what: Writes automated tests that click through the app and check it works.
day: Writes end-to-end and API tests
Spins up the app with test data
Chases flaky tests

roles.name: Benchmark / Performance Engineer
roles.what: Writes and runs benchmarks to find what is slow and prove a fix worked.
day: Writes load and speed tests
Runs them on clean, repeatable setups
Reads traces and graphs to find the slow part

roles.name: Contract / Integration Test Engineer
roles.what: Makes sure services agree on how they talk, before they break each other.
day: Writes contract tests between services
Mocks other teams' APIs from specs
Checks changes will not break callers

roles.name: Security Engineer (AppSec)
roles.what: Finds and fixes security holes in code and dependencies.
day: Reviews code and designs for risks
Runs scanners on code, images and packages
Helps teams fix findings and rotate secrets

roles.name: DevSecOps Engineer
roles.what: Builds security checks into pipelines so bad code never ships.
day: Adds scanners and signing to CI
Manages secrets and access
Tracks what is inside every release

roles.name: Resilience / Chaos Test Engineer
roles.what: Breaks things on purpose to see if the system copes.
day: Adds slow and failing networks to tests
Kills services and checks recovery
Writes down what failed and how to fix it

roles.name: Forward Deployed Engineer
roles.what: Sits with a customer and ships working software inside their setup, fast.
day: Gets a customer's stack running locally
Builds the demo or integration
Fixes what breaks in their environment

roles.name: Solutions Engineer
roles.what: Shows the product to buyers, builds proof-of-concept demos, answers hard questions.
day: Runs live demos and tailors them
Builds quick proof-of-concept apps
Answers technical questions from buyers

roles.name: Developer Advocate / DevRel
roles.what: Teaches developers to use the product with talks, demos, samples and docs.
day: Builds sample apps and tutorials
Gives talks and records demos
Takes developer feedback back to the team

roles.name: Support Engineer
roles.what: Helps customers fix technical problems and finds bugs in the product.
day: Reproduces a customer's bug
Reads logs and traces
Writes the bug report for engineers

roles.name: Integration Engineer
roles.what: Connects the product to a customer's other systems through APIs and webhooks.
day: Maps data between systems
Tests webhooks from a laptop
Mocks partner APIs that are not ready

roles.name: Tech Lead
roles.what: Leads a team's code, reviews work and keeps the local setup and CI healthy.
day: Reviews pull requests and sets standards
Splits work and unblocks others
Keeps new-hire setup and CI working

roles.name: Staff Engineer
roles.what: Solves the hard cross-team problems and sets technical direction.
day: Writes design docs and decides trade-offs
Picks tools that many teams will share
Digs into the worst bugs and slowdowns

roles.name: Software Architect
roles.what: Draws how systems fit together and picks the building blocks.
day: Designs services, data flow and boundaries
Compares frameworks and cloud services
Checks the design against real constraints

roles.name: Engineering Manager
roles.what: Manages people and delivery. Watches team health, not code.
day: Runs 1:1s, planning and hiring
Tracks delivery and removes blockers
Reads dashboards to spot risk early

roles.name: Open-source Maintainer
roles.what: Keeps a public project alive. Reviews contributions, cuts releases, fights spam.
day: Reviews pull requests from strangers
Cuts releases and writes changelogs
Makes it easy for new people to contribute

levels.name: Package Wrangler
levels.goal: Install, pin and update dependencies without breaking your teammates.

flisk.text: Flisk does not touch package managers yet. Coming soon.

levels.name: Build Master
levels.goal: Turn source into fast, cached, repeatable builds and tasks.

flisk.text: Flisk generates per-service Vite and TSConfig config from the manifests. It does not run your build graph.

levels.name: Container Crafter
levels.goal: Package any service as an image and run a few of them together.

flisk.text: Flisk generates the Compose config and layered base images from each service's manifest.

levels.name: Inner-Loop Runner
levels.goal: Edit code and see it live across many services in seconds.

flisk.text: This is Flisk's core: `flisk up` discovers services and runs them with live reload on Tilt.

levels.name: Cluster Tamer
levels.goal: Develop against Kubernetes, locally or bridged to a shared cluster.

flisk.text: Flisk is local only today and emits no Kubernetes manifests. Coming soon.

levels.name: Agent Wrangler
levels.goal: Run multi-agent systems with tools, memory and models on your own machine.

flisk.text: Flisk has an agent resource type with health, readiness and stored sessions, an MCP server and an agent-stack starter.

levels.name: Platform Architect
levels.goal: Give every team golden paths, a portal and infrastructure as code.

flisk.text: Flisk has no Backstage plugin or IaC export yet. Coming soon.

tracks.name: Backend
tracks.blurb: APIs, workers and databases, from one service to a dozen.

package-wrangler.tip: Pick one package manager per language and commit the lockfile.

build-master.tip: Make every build and test runnable with one short command.

container-crafter.tip: One Dockerfile per service, one Compose file for all of them.

inner-loop-runner.tip: Aim for a save-to-running loop under five seconds.

cluster-tamer.tip: Only reach for Kubernetes locally when production runs on it.

agent-wrangler.tip: Treat the agent like another service with health checks and logs.

platform-architect.tip: Write down the path you took so the next team gets it for free.

tracks.name: AI & agents
tracks.blurb: Multi-agent systems with tools, memory, models and traces.

package-wrangler.tip: Python and Node both show up in agent stacks; pin both runtimes.

build-master.tip: Keep prompts and tool schemas in the repo, built and versioned like code.

container-crafter.tip: Put every tool server and database in a container so agents can reach them.

inner-loop-runner.tip: Restart one agent without losing the others' state.

cluster-tamer.tip: Agents rarely need Kubernetes locally; skip ahead if production does not use it.

agent-wrangler.tip: Persist checkpoints outside the process so a restart does not lose a session.

platform-architect.tip: Give every agent the same contract for health, sessions and traces.

tracks.name: Platform
tracks.blurb: Golden paths, portals and shared environments for many teams.

package-wrangler.tip: Standardize runtime versions before you standardize anything else.

build-master.tip: Remote caching pays for itself as soon as CI is the bottleneck.

container-crafter.tip: Publish blessed base images and keep them patched.

inner-loop-runner.tip: The inner loop is a product; measure time to first change for new hires.

cluster-tamer.tip: Give each developer an isolated namespace or virtual cluster.

agent-wrangler.tip: Ship MCP servers for your internal tools so agents use the same golden paths.

platform-architect.tip: A portal is only as good as the templates and docs behind it.
